headline: Prince Harry went to Ukraine to cheer wounded soldiers.
summary: Prince Harry spent two days in Lviv, Ukraine, with wounded soldiers training for his Invictus Games. The trip stayed secret until he had left. Ukraine has more than 150,000 injured veterans. He watched wheelchair rugby, played pickleball and met a soldier who walks again with a spinal implant. "You're going to win the war," he told them.

cover_question.q: Why did a prince go to a war?

cover_answer: Not to fight. To visit soldiers who got hurt.
table_question: If a friend is hurt, is showing up enough, or do you have to help?

5-7.script: A prince from England named Harry flew to Ukraine, a country at war, to visit soldiers who got hurt. He watched them play rugby in wheelchairs, crashing into each other like bumper cars. Then they all cheered his name and crowded in for selfies. He has left Ukraine now, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: The wheelchair rugby is the picture. The war stays behind it.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old takes one vivid picture, so the script hands them wheelchairs crashing like bumper cars, not the war that put the men in them. What frightens a child this age is what they can see, so the slide shows a cheering gym and says the prince has left. Expect "did the soldiers get better?" Some walk again. Some won't.

8-12.script: Ukraine has more than 150,000 wounded soldiers. Prince Harry runs the Invictus Games, sports for wounded troops, and 400 Ukrainians are trying out for next year's. His trip stayed secret until he'd left, the way a surprise party only works if nobody knows.
8-12.why: Wounded soldiers, a sports contest, a secret trip: a chain.
8-12.why_long: At nine a child is working out cause and effect, so the script runs the chain: a war, 150,000 wounded, doctors who became the experts, a prince with a games for them. The surprise party explains the press blackout without the word missile. Expect "why was it secret?" Russia fires at Ukraine. Nobody could aim at a secret.

13-17.script: Does a famous visitor help a country at war, or mostly himself? Prince Harry got a huge welcome in Lviv and told wounded veterans "you're going to win the war". Second: Ukraine's doctors now teach the world about trauma, he said. Who wants that expertise?
13-17.why: A cheer he can't back up, and expertise bought with blood.
13-17.why_long: A thirteen-year-old can hold two true things at once: a prince with no army promising a win, and a welcome that was real. Then: Ukraine has the best trauma doctors, and the reason is 150,000 wounded. Kuhn found arguing is a practised skill; the question is a case. Expect "can he promise that?" No. He can promise to keep showing up.

5-7.q: Why did a prince go to a war?
5-7.a: To visit soldiers who got hurt and cheer them on. He didn't go to fight, and he has left now.

8-12.q: Why was the trip a secret?
8-12.a: Russia fires missiles at Ukraine. The visit was announced only after he left.
Sports for wounded soldiers, started by Harry. 400 Ukrainians are in trials.

13-17.q: Can he actually promise they'll win?
13-17.a: No. He has no army. He promised support, and a games there after the war.

13-17.q: How does a soldier walk with an implant?
13-17.a: A spinal stimulator, recharged every 12 hours. He steers with his eyes.
